Paratus Energy: Q3 2026 Results

Paratus Energy: Q3 2026 Results

PR Newswire

HAMILTON, Bermuda, Nov. 27, 2026

HAMILTON, Bermuda, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Paratus Energy Services Ltd. (OSLO: PLSV) ("Paratus" or the "Company") today reported operational and financial results for the third quarter of 2026, highlighted by $79 million in combined segment revenues and $50 million in adjusted EBITDA, from continuing operations. The Company and its ownership in Seagems ended the quarter with $169 million in cash and a net debt of $239 million (1.3x leverage).

Paratus is pleased to announce that its Board of Directors (the "Board") has authorized a quarterly cash distribution of $0.22 per share for Q3 2026, consistent with prior quarters.

Q3 2026 highlights, including notable post-quarter developments:

  • Recently announced a strategic review of the Company's investment in the Seagems JV.
  • Successfully completed the Fontis sale and used cash proceeds received at closing towards partial redemption of bonds.
  • Delivered strong operational performance, with PLSV fleet technical utilization of approximately 99%.
  • Reported combined segment revenue and EBITDA of $79 million and $50 million, respectively.
  • Closed the quarter with combined cash of $169 million and net debt of $239 million (1.3x net leverage ratio).
  • Seagems was recently awarded a four-year contract for the third-party horizontal pipelaying vessel Safira.
  • Petrobras recently confirmed the acceptance of Seagems' bid for a four-year contract for Jade.
  • Post Q3, declared $0.22 per share dividend for Q3 2026, consistent with previous quarters.

Corporate and operational review for the third quarter of 2026

Strategic review of investment in the Seagems JV

On November 18, 2026, Paratus announced a strategic review of its investment in Seagems. Paratus and Vantris Energy Berhad ("Vantris") are conducting the review on a coordinated basis and exploring third-party interest in the Seagems business as a whole.

Pareto Securities is acting as financial adviser to Paratus, while J.P. Morgan is acting as financial adviser to Vantris. The review may or may not lead to a transaction, and no decision to transact has been taken by either of the two joint venture parties at this stage.

The Company will provide further updates as appropriate and in accordance with its disclosure obligations under applicable law.

Seagems operating and financial update

Paratus' 50% share in the Seagems joint venture contributed $78.6 million in contract revenues, compared with $71 million in the prior quarter. The quarter-over-quarter increase was primarily driven by the recovery from planned maintenance activities and operational incidents involving Esmeralda and Jade during the prior quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $51.1 million, up from $43.5 million in the prior quarter.

The JV achieved technical utilization of 98.6% (Q2 2026: 93.7%) and the contract backlog at quarter-end was approximately $0.9 billion (Q2 2026: approximately $1.1 billion), excluding the subsequent Safira award.

During the quarter, Seagems distributed $34.8 million to Paratus (Q2 2026: $30.2 million).

Earlier in 2026, Petrobras launched a PLSV tender for contracts commencing in 2028, comprising five lots with varying technical specifications and offering contract durations of four years. Seagems submitted bids for the Jade and a third-party vessel to which it had secured exclusive access in the event of a contract award.

On November 17, 2026, the Company announced that Seagems had been awarded a four-year contract with Petrobras for the third-party horizontal pipelaying vessel Safira, which is currently under construction. The contract is expected to commence in Q4 2028 and is expected to add approximately $410 million to Seagems' backlog, of which the Company has a 50% share.

Seagems has secured access to the vessel through a memorandum of understanding ("MOU"), which includes a purchase option. While the timing remains subject to change, Seagems currently expects to conclude on whether to acquire the vessel before year-end or early next year. If acquired, Safira would become the seventh owned vessel in Seagems' fleet and be expected to contribute significant operating cash flow once operations under the Petrobras contract commence.

Safira will have a horizontal pipelaying system ("HLS") with 300-tonne tension capacity. The Company believes that Safira is unlikely to target the more technically demanding, higher-tension deepwater projects that the high-specification 550-tonne PLSVs with vertical pipelaying systems (VLS) in Seagems' existing fleet are well suited for. Due to differences in vessel dimensions, tonnage, equipment configuration and operational capabilities, Safira's estimated construction cost is materially lower than the estimated replacement cost of Seagems' existing high-specification 550-tonne PLSVs.

The JV continues to explore opportunities to expand the Seagems business and leverage its established operational platform. This work is ongoing, and the Company believes that there is meaningful potential for further growth.

On November 9, 2026, the Company announced that Petrobras had published its final tender results, confirming the acceptance of Seagems' bid for the Jade PLSV. The prospective four-year contract is expected to commence in Q1 2028 and remains subject to formal award by Petrobras and the execution of definitive agreements. While no firm agreements are in place, we currently expect that the vessel will be employed during the time between the expiration of the current contract and the start-up of the prospective four-year contract with Petrobras.

Market outlook

On November 23, 2026, Petrobras announced its 2027-2031 business plan, providing for total capital expenditure of $122 billion, approximately 12% above the $109 billion included in its 2026-2030 plan. E&P remains the principal investment area, accounting for more than 70% of planned expenditure. The plan also indicates estimated demand for approximately 7,000 km of rigid and flexible pipelines and umbilicals, including installations and recoveries, compared with approximately 6,000 km in the previous plan. Overall, we believe the increased investment and activity levels are supportive of the demand outlook for subsea support vessels, including PLSVs, in Brazil.

Webcast

Paratus will host a presentation of the Q3 2026 results via an audio webcast today at 15:00 CET. To join the webcast, please use the following link:

https://paratusenergy.engagestream.euronext.com/q3-2026

For further information, please contact:

About Paratus

Paratus Energy Services Ltd. (OSLO: PLSV) is an investment holding company with a 50% joint venture interest in Seagems. Seagems is a leading subsea services company that owns and operates a fleet of six multi-purpose pipe-laying support vessels, providing support, installation, flexible pipe-laying and construction services. All vessels are currently operating under contracts in Brazil.

data.title: aphranel® Advances Clinical Exploration of CaHA Biostructurer at European Scientific Advisory Board in Paris
data.description:
aphranel® Advances Clinical Exploration of CaHA Biostructurer at European Scientific Advisory Board in Paris

aphranel® Advances Clinical Exploration of CaHA Biostructurer at European Scientific Advisory Board in Paris

PR Newswire

PARIS, Nov. 27, 2026

European Advisory Board and Cadaver Workshop bring together international expertise, anatomical insights and Chinese-developed CaHA innovation.

PARIS, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- aphranel®, the regenerative aesthetics brand developed by MOYOM Biotech, convened leading European aesthetic medicine experts in Paris on October 16–17, 2026, for its European Scientific Advisory Board and Cadaver Workshop.

Chaired by internationally recognized plastic surgeon Dr. Patrick Trévidic, the two-day programme marked an important step in exploring how aphranel®'s Biostructurer concept can be translated from biomaterial science into anatomy-based clinical practice.

The two-day programme brought together experts from different medical specialties to examine the scientific foundations of CaHA biostructuring, review clinical experience from China and discuss its potential applications in European aesthetic medicine.

At the centre of the discussions was a fundamental question: How can structural support, collagen biostimulation and controlled biodegradation be considered together in the development of individualized aesthetic treatment strategies?

Built on more than 13 years of biomaterial research and development, aphranel® incorporates proprietary calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) microsphere technology within its MagiCCrystal CaHA Biostructurer. Its porous microsphere architecture and gel carrier system are designed to combine structural support with collagen biostimulation and biodegradation over time, reflecting the brand's broader philosophy of The Poetics of Time.

The advisory board examined these material characteristics alongside clinical observations, patient assessment, injection techniques and safety considerations, emphasizing the importance of evidence-based clinical evaluation.

The international faculty included:

  • Dr. Patrick Trévidic, a Paris-based plastic surgeon and co-founder of Expert2Expert;
  • Dr. Víctor Hernández Machado, a plastic and aesthetic surgeon and Medical Director of Cànons Clinics in Spain;
  • Dr. Tiago Nogueira Guimarães, a UK GMC-registered plastic surgeon with extensive NHS experience;
  • Dr. Rouzbeh Karimi, an ENT and head and neck surgery specialist based in Hungary.

Their diverse clinical perspectives encouraged critical discussions on the evaluation and adaption of treatment approaches and clinical experience across different medical practices.

The second day extended scientific discussions into a comparative cadaver workshop, connecting clinical perspectives with direct anatomical observation.

Through injection demonstrations, dissection and structured assessments, participating physicians explored product placement, tissue distribution and anatomical relationships involving facial ligaments, fat compartments and vascular structures.

The workshop reinforced one of Biostructurer's central principles: understanding facial anatomy before planning structural correction. By integrating case-based discussions with anatomical assessment, the programme helped identify clinical considerations and areas requiring further investigation.

Building Long-Term Scientific Collaboration in Europe

The Paris programme represents another step in aphranel®'s international scientific development, following China's NMPA Class III medical device approval in 2025 and EU MDR certification in 2026.

Supported by its strategic collaboration with Expert2Expert (E2E), the initiative forms part of aphranel®'s broader commitment to international medical education and clinical exchange.

Through The Norns' Weave, its international academic initiative, aphranel® aims to facilitate ongoing dialogue between Chinese and European physicians, connecting clinical experience, scientific research and professional education.

Looking ahead, MOYOM Biotech plans to expand European clinical evidence development, expert collaboration and anatomy-based educational programmes, supporting a deeper scientific understanding of CaHA biostructuring and its clinical potential.

More than a scientific gathering, the Paris programme reflects a long-term commitment to bringing Chinese biomaterial innovation into international clinical dialogue. Where scientific concepts are critically examined, clinical knowledge is shared and evidence continues to evolve.

About aphranel®

aphranel® is a regenerative aesthetics brand developed by MOYOM Biotech. Built on proprietary CaHA microsphere and gel technology, its MagiCCrystal CaHA Biostructurer combines structural support, collagen biostimulation and biodegradation. Guided by The Poetics of Time and a commitment to long-termism, aphranel® continues to advance biomaterial research, clinical collaboration and international medical education.

data.title: Asian Markets Rise as AI Sentiment Stabilizes — Update
data.description:
By Sherry Qin and Kimberley Kao

Asian markets rose on Friday, tracking gains in U.S. stock futures as sentiment around the artificial intelligence trade stabilized.

"With U.S. bourses shut for Thanksgiving, global stocks mostly rose in the absence of cues," Maybank analysts said in a note.

That has left "markets to trade largely off the late recovery on Wall Street in Wednesday's session," said Westpac's Neha Sharma in an email.

Regional investors took cues from stronger U.S. futures. E-mini Nasdaq futures were up 2.6%, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.7% and 1.1%, respectively.

South Korea's Kospi rose 4.2%, with chip heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics jumping 6.3% and 4.2%, respectively.

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average advanced 2.0%. SoftBank Group was last 3.7% higher, while chip players Resonac Holdings and Advantest surged 9.7% and 6.0% respectively.

The gains came even as Nvidia ordered its manufacturing partners to pause shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, after the U.S. escalated its push to keep the company's AI chips out of China's hands, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Meanwhile, China's State Council on Friday reinforced its support for the capital market and stressed the need to improve market-stabilizing mechanisms. It also said that listed companies should be encouraged to pay more dividends and step up share repurchases.

China's Shanghai Composite Index rose 3.2%, while tech-heavy ChiNext Price Index jumped 10%, keeping it on track for its biggest one-day gain in over two years.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 2.3% higher, while the Hang Seng Tech Index rose 6.3% and Taiwan's Taiex was up by 0.4%.

The three-month LME copper contract jumped 4.6% to $12,423.00 a ton. Copper prices are supported by strong near-term AI spending expectations, according to ANZ research analysts in a commentary. Copper is a key metal for data center development.

Spot gold rose 2.0% to $3,638.54 a troy ounce while spot silver rose 5.0% to $43.60 a troy ounce. Bitcoin rose 1.6%.

Oil prices jumped on fresh concerns of a re-escalation of tensions in the Middle East. Iran has stepped up its strikes, targeting some of its Gulf neighbors and ships trying to get oil and natural gas through the Strait of Hormuz. Most recently, an Iranian drone attack on Kuwait killed two Italians performing maintenance on antidrone equipment, authorities said.

Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthi militant group attacked Saudi Arabia's Jazan oil refinery on Thursday and killed one worker, the kingdom's Ministry of Energy said in a statement.

The attacks offset hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, ANZ Research analysts said in a note.

However, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week in the seven days through Nov. 20, while gasoline and distillate stockpiles also increased, according to the latest data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude-oil futures rose 3.3% to $86.43 a barrel, while front-month Brent was up 0.9% at $97.41 a barrel, according to ICE data.

data.title: NEW ART HOLDINGS Introduces a New Kind of Brilliance: The “Shining” Jewelry Collection Launches Tomorrow
data.description:
• Inspired by “Sun Glitter,” the mesmerizing play of sunlight across rippling water.
  • Four exquisite designs featuring the finest ULTIMATE MELEE® diamonds, brought to life through delicate, graceful movement.

TOKYO, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NEW ART HOLDINGS Co., Ltd. (TSE Standard Market: 7638) (“NEW ART” or the “Company”), the parent company of a leading Japanese bridal jewelry group operating the EXELCO DIAMOND and GINZA DIAMOND SHIRAISHI brands, today announced that its new “Shining” collection of four diamond necklaces will debut on Saturday, November 28, 2026, in time for the holiday season. The collection will be available at GINZA DIAMOND SHIRAISHI boutiques across Japan. Drawing on its heritage as a leading bridal jewelry specialist in Japan, the brand brings its signature craftsmanship to this new collection.

Designed as meaningful gifts to mark life’s special moments—from wedding anniversaries and birthdays to the joy of welcoming a child—the collection offers fine diamond necklaces that complement both everyday styles and bridal rings.

Inspired by “Sun Glitter,” the mesmerizing sparkle of sunlight that dances across ocean waves, the collection captures the fleeting beauty of light in motion. Each pendant features ULTIMATE MELEE® diamonds, selected to meet the rigorous quality standards of the brand’s bridal rings. Suspended in a delicate swing setting, the diamonds move gracefully with the wearer, catching the light from every angle and creating an ever-changing brilliance.

Collection Highlights

  • Bridal-Ring Standards of Excellence: ULTIMATE MELEE® Diamonds
    Every necklace features ULTIMATE MELEE® diamonds, selected according to the same rigorous quality standards applied to GINZA DIAMOND SHIRAISHI’s bridal rings. Only diamonds graded F color or higher and VVS clarity or higher are chosen, helping to ensure remarkable transparency and brilliance.
    To showcase their remarkable clarity and fire, each design features a focal diamond measuring 2.9 mm in diameter—the largest size classification among melee diamonds.
  • Four Expressions of “Sun Glitter” in a Graceful Swing Setting
    The collection captures the fleeting beauty of sunlight shimmering across the ocean, scattering into countless pools of light that shift and dance with the movement of the waves. By designing the diamond settings with a freely swinging structure, the diamonds move delicately with the wearer's natural movements, continuously catching and reflecting light at the neckline.
  • Thoughtful Craftsmanship in Every Detail
    Every element has been carefully considered to achieve a balance of refined aesthetics, functionality, and lasting beauty.

    • Star-Inspired Diamond Setting Backs: Inspired by the sparkle of Sun Glitter, the back openings of the diamond settings are specially crafted into curved, star-like rhombus shapes.
    • Minimalist Connecting Rings: The connecting rings are designed to be as discreet as possible, keeping the diamonds as the visual focal point while maintaining the strength and security required for everyday wear.
    • Delicately Radiant Chain: Each necklace is finished with a finely faceted Azuki chain (0.23 gauge) that adds a subtle shimmer of its own. The 45 cm chain features a 5 cm adjustment ring, allowing it to be worn at either 45 cm or 40 cm.

  • Available Materials and Specifications
    All four designs are available in three material options: Platinum (Pt850/Pt950); 18K Yellow Gold (K18YG); 18K Pink Gold (K18PG). The chain is a finely faceted Azuki chain, 0.23 gauge with a 45 cm total length, and a 5 cm adjustment ring to wear at 40 cm.

The Four Designs

Shining Glint


Inspired by a single, brilliant flash of sunlight across the rippling water, “Glint” captures the beauty of a single, brilliant sparkle.

  • Platinum (Pt850/Pt950): ¥223,500 (tax included)
  • 18K Yellow Gold (K18YG) / 18K Pink Gold (K18PG): ¥273,000 (tax included)

Shining Road


Inspired by the breathtaking natural phenomenon when sunlight stretches across the sea, creating a luminous pathway that extends endlessly over the water.

  • Platinum (Pt850/Pt950): ¥242,500 (tax included)
  • 18K Yellow Gold (K18YG) / 18K Pink Gold (K18PG): ¥294,000 (tax included)

Shining Drop

A serene expression of light, evoking the quiet beauty of a single dewdrop formed amid gentle, calming waves.

  • Platinum (Pt850/Pt950): ¥251,000 (tax included)
  • 18K Yellow Gold (K18YG) / 18K Pink Gold (K18PG): ¥303,000 (tax included)

Shining Veil

Evoking a delicate veil of sunlight that softly spreads and shimmers across the ever-moving surface of the sea.

  • Platinum (Pt850/Pt950): ¥277,500 (tax included)
  • 18K Yellow Gold (K18YG) / 18K Pink Gold (K18PG): ¥331,000 (tax included)

About NEW ART HOLDINGS Co., Ltd.

Founded in September 1994 and headquartered in Ginza, Tokyo, NEW ART HOLDINGS Co., Ltd. (TSE Standard Market: 7638) is a leading specialist in bridal diamond jewelry in Japan, guided by the philosophy: “We harness the transformative power of art to inspire beauty, health, and happiness.” The Group operates a diversified portfolio spanning bridal jewelry, fine art, auction services, health & beauty, the food business in Hong Kong, and apparel across 17 consolidated subsidiaries — nine domestic and eight international.

The Group's flagship jewelry brands, GINZA DIAMOND SHIRAISHI and EXELCO DIAMOND, operate 154 stores globally — 128 across Japan and 26 internationally, spanning Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore and South Korea.

For more information, please visit: www.newart-ir.jp.

data.title: EMEA Morning Briefing: Stock Futures Rise as AI Sentiment Stabilizes
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

Watch For:

EU economic sentiment; Germany jobless rate; France CPI, consumer spending; No major corporate trading updates expected

Opening Call:

European stock futures traded higher early Friday. Asian stock benchmarks were up; the dollar strengthened; Treasury yields were higher; while oil futures and gold rose.

Equities:

Stock futures point to a higher open in Europe, tracking gains in U.S. stock futures as sentiment around artificial intelligence stabilized.

"U.S. markets were closed for Thanksgiving, leaving global markets to trade largely off the late recovery on Wall Street in Wednesday's session," said Westpac's Neha Sharma.

Forex:

The euro was modestly higher against the dollar, after news that European governments picked Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos to be the next president of the European Central Bank.

Their choice didn't come as a surprise, as he was considered a front-runner for the role. In 2024, Hernandez de Cos joked that he was an "owl" when asked whether he was a "hawk" or "dove," emphasizing his focus on data rather than leaning in favor of tightening or loosening policy.

Bonds:

Minutes from the ECB's October meeting confirm that an interest-rate increase in December appears likely, ING's Carsten Brzeski said.

While the central bank voted to keep rates unchanged, several members openly advocated for a hike. This sends a clear signal that a rate increase on Dec. 18 is a done deal if inflation concerns remain elevated, Brzeski said.

But the path is less clear beyond December. Much will depend on the pass-through of energy prices to other areas of the economy, Brzeski said, adding that additional hikes in 2027 could do more harm than good.

Energy:

An attack by the Houthis on an oil refinery in Jazan in Saudi Arabia halted some operations there. Rising attacks on energy infrastructure across the Middle East have raised concerns of further supply disruptions, ANZ Research analysts said.

However, the latest U.S. data showed that commercial crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week, while gasoline and distillate stockpiles also increased.

Metals:

Near-term pressure on gold might persist until equities stabilize, said HSBC analyst James Steel.

"Continued equity market weakness puts gold at risk of breaking the next major support level at $3,400 an ounce," he said. Still, gold appears undervalued and any sign of central-bank buying could arrest declines, Steel said. Copper rose in Asian trading. Prices were supported by strong near-term AI spending expectations, ANZ research analysts said. Copper is a key metal for data-center development.

Spending on data centers and other AI-related infrastructure is likely to remain strong in the next few quarters, the analysts said. Iron ore prices were lower in Asian trading, weighed by supply growth and weak demand.

Production ramp-up is progressing smoothly, Xingye Futures analysts said. However, winter restocking by steel mills and support from global miners' marginal production costs might provide near-term price support, they added. The brokerage maintains a cautiously bearish outlook, with attention on the pace of winter restocking and the strength of cost support.

TODAY'S TOP HEADLINES

Stocks' Swoon and Higher Interest Rates Are a Bad Combo for the Economy

"Engine" Charlie Wilson may be best remembered for being misquoted as asserting that what was good for General Motors was good for the country. There is no doubt about President Donald Trump's view, as he wrote on Truth Social that Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive of Nvidia is vital "to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."

And, he might have added, the stock market, a major driver of financial conditions, on which the economy depends and that is also never far from the president's focus.

Europe Has Picked a New Central Bank Chief. He's in for a Bumpy Ride.

BRUSSELS-European leaders have chosen Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to be the next president of the European Central Bank, betting a technocrat can navigate the continent through debt problems in France, flagging growth and stock-market jitters.

Hernández de Cos will succeed departing President Christine Lagarde, who is stepping down in February. The European Parliament and the ECB's governing council must endorse his candidacy, with a final seal of approval by EU leaders expected in December.

No Homes to Rent, No Way to Evict: Inside Spain's Housing Crisis

MADRID-In the spring of 2024, Sonia Moreira told her tenant of over a decade that she planned to sell her property, a top-floor, redbrick apartment in a working-class area outside the Spanish capital.

The tenant, Helizabet Delgado, refused to leave and stopped paying rent. Unemployed and facing health issues, she has benefited from housing laws designed to protect vulnerable tenants from eviction.

Nvidia Tells Partners to Pause Shipments to Southeast Asia

Nvidia ordered its manufacturing partners to pause shipments to four Southeast Asian countries after the U.S. escalated its push to keep the company's AI chips out of China's hands.

The chip maker instructed Dell, Super Micro Computer and other manufacturers to stop server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia for an unspecified period, a person familiar with the matter said. Chinese companies have drawn a portion of their computing power by remotely accessing Nvidia chips in data centers in those countries.

Marlboro Maker Altria Explores Deal for Rival Imperial Brands

Altria said it was considering a cash bid to buy smaller London-listed peer Imperial Brands, a move that would expand the Marlboro maker's footprint selling cigarettes around the world.

Altria, based in Richmond, Va., has a market value of close to $127 billion and offers a range of brands including Marlboro cigarettes in the U.S., Skoal smokeless tobacco and NJOY e-cigarettes.

data.title: AIPro Supplies AI Video Analytics to Public Facilities and Power Plants, Expanding Site-Specific Safety Management
data.description:
AIPro Supplies AI Video Analytics to Public Facilities and Power Plants, Expanding Site-Specific Safety Management

AIPro Supplies AI Video Analytics to Public Facilities and Power Plants, Expanding Site-Specific Safety Management

PR Newswire

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 26, 2026

Fire monitoring at the KAMCO Human Resources Development Institute and person detection in the discharge zone at Goesan Hydropower Plant; on-device video analytics research also underway

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AIPro, an AI video analytics company, is expanding the use of its CCTV analytics technology to address site-specific safety challenges at public facilities and power plants. From software that detects signs of fires and wildfires to a system that detects people in a dam's downstream discharge zone, the company provides solutions tailored to each site's needs.

According to AIPro, the company has supplied fire and wildfire detection software to the Korea Asset Management Corporation (KAMCO) Human Resources Development Institute and VistaPro-FDS-002, a fire detection solution designated as an innovative product, to the Korea Gas Safety Corporation. At Goesan Hydropower Plant, operated by Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power, the company supplied a system that detects people in the dam's downstream discharge zone.

Each deployment uses CCTV video analytics for a distinct safety management objective. In fire monitoring, the focus is on detecting signs of fire, such as flames and smoke, in CCTV footage; in the discharge zone, the focus is on detecting the presence of people. The company explained that it tailors its video analytics capabilities to the monitoring requirements and operational objectives of each site.

VistaPro, the company's platform for enterprises and institutions, supports flame and smoke detection, people counting, and detection of people approaching or entering restricted areas, depending on the site configuration. AI-powered analysis helps managers assess on-site conditions and determine whether a response is needed. The platform is designed to reduce the workload of managers who must continuously monitor multiple CCTV feeds.

AIPro was founded in 2020 by Professor Chun-Su Park of Sungkyunkwan University. It translates research in computer vision and image processing into products that support safety management and operations at public facilities and industrial sites. The enterprise and institutional version of VistaPro has earned Grade 1 Good Software (GS) certification, and VistaPro-FDS-002 has been designated as an innovative product by the Public Procurement Service. The company's AI video analytics models have also undergone performance testing by the Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA).

The company's research and development efforts focus on improving both detection performance and operational efficiency. Building on its patented technology for improving the computational efficiency of video surveillance systems, the company continues to develop products that account for on-site imaging conditions and the computational load on hardware.

Through the "Super-Gap Startup 1000+" program, the company is currently developing an on-device software engine capable of running multiple deep learning models on devices deployed in the field. It is also conducting research on ultra-long-range object detection and low-power optimization. In addition, the company is participating in a project to develop and demonstrate an integrated AI-based system for early fire detection and suppression in livestock barns, gaining practical experience in field operations.

AIPro plans to draw on its experience deploying solutions at public institutions and conducting research and development to improve its products and expand adoption across sites of various sizes. By addressing site-specific needs such as fire monitoring, people counting, and restricted-area management, the company aims to help users in Korea and abroad adopt video analytics technology suited to their operational needs and scale.
